findings.finding: Terminal verdict USDA live_canary contradicts its own evidence. Verdict states 'historical probes wasde0512/wasde0115 (0512 PASS, 0115 measured 404 recorded honestly)' but usda_wasde_summary.json records wasde0512 as BLOCKED_NETWORK http_status 404, raw_sha256 NOT_APPLIED (no success anywhere in summary/manifest/disk). Verdict's 'current releases (0926/0826 xml/txt/xls)' and 'recent 2 releases' imply two releases acquired; manifest + raw root contain ONLY wasde0826 (txt/xls/xml, 3 artifacts) - wasde0926 links are inventoried, never downloaded. 2010s samples: both probes (0512, 0115) measured 404, zero acquired. Underlying artifacts are honest; the verdict narrative overstates measured coverage.

Terminal verdict SEC FTD inventory claim '434 zip archives cnsfails{YYYYMM}{a,b}.zip 2008-01 -> 2026-08' is wrong on the start bound. The manifest (sorted by dataset_id) begins at monthly_cnsfails200907a; regex finds NO monthly_cnsfails2008xx and no 2009-01..2009-06 records; the raw directory contains no cnsfails2008*.zip and the earliest bytes are cnsfails200907a.zip. Actual acquired coverage starts 2009-07, ~18 months later than the frozen claim. The count 434 is correct (434 monthly_ records + 1 inventory = 435 manifest records).

'0 sequence gaps' (Coinbase) and '0 gaps' (Kraken) in the verdict and stream summaries are vacuous metrics, not measured continuity. kraken.py sequence_of() returns None unconditionally (comment: crc continuity 'judged at analysis time, not capture time'); coinbase.py sequence_of() never matched (every channel in the Coinbase summary has last_sequence null across 10353 messages, so no sequence was ever extracted). Only Deribit book channels had real sequence accounting (change_id, regression-only gap rule). The verdict presents gap-free capture for Coinbase/Kraken as if measured.
